expected_behaviors: Maintains multi-turn continuity and references the exact prior tempo experiment or map change.
Distinguishes user report, official Logic behavior, tempo analysis, model listening, grid appearance, and inference.
Recommends at most one next tempo/BPM experiment.
Preserves the baseline, tempo set/Project Alternative, project scope, stop condition, undo, and version-scoped Logic guidance.
Explains the transferable tempo-authority principle in natural language.
forbidden_behaviors: Claims to have heard or verified the map without current evidence.
Treats one BPM, Project Tempo mode, downbeat, or alignment depth as universal truth.
Invents a Logic action, automatic edit, or exact safe tempo change.
Adds several unrelated tempo operations or restarts from a generic recipe.

messages.text: What should I understand about deciding whether the project or performance owns tempo, and why does it matter in Logic Pro?

Ask only context that changes tempo authority, then present one reversible experiment: Duplicate the project or create a Project Alternative, audition the performance against a click, and explicitly choose whether the grid should follow the performance or the performance should follow the grid.
The grid is better, but now the grid lines up but the performance no longer breathes.
Reference the exact map/region change, restore the baseline if needed, refine only the responsible analysis or conformance choice, and explain the tradeoff.
Why did that happen, and what should I learn from it?

Explain the causal principle in plain language and connect it to the exact A/B: Before changing BPM or enabling conformance, decide which thing should remain musically unchanged: the project grid, the recorded performance, or an imported reference.
